Cabinet clears eastern rail corridor

The union cabinet approved a new eastern freight rail corridor on Tuesday, clearing the way for construction to begin in the next financial year, according to a statement issued after the meeting.

The corridor will run for roughly nine hundred kilometres and is intended to move coal and container traffic away from passenger lines that have been operating close to capacity for several years.

Officials said the project would be funded through a mix of budgetary support and borrowing, with the first tranche released in the coming quarter once tendering is complete and land acquisition has been settled in the three affected states.

Short aside.

An industry group welcomed the decision but cautioned that similar corridors had slipped well past their announced timelines, and said the schedule would depend on how quickly environmental clearances were granted along the route.
